<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Plan 235 compiles each page in with `include_str!`, so a page is its file at build time. Between builds they drift: an edited page reads the old text until pij-rs is rebuilt. The stage reads what the binary actually prints, so `harness checks --quick` (which skips the Rust build) fails on an edited page until it is rebuilt, and a full `harness checks` passes only once the binary it built carries the edit. `pij docs list --json` names each page's source file, so the check restates no table.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A page that differs from its file cannot pass `harness checks`.
- The check reads the producer: what pij-rs prints and which file it names, never a second list.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Checking the pij-rs installed on PATH: a branch that edits a page would fail against the installed main build until it merged and installed. Open question q-1.
- The pages themselves (step s03).

<a id="research-context"></a>

## Research Context

Sensors live in `.harness/extensions/checks/extension.ts` (SENSORS) and `just self-check`, added together (AGENTS.md). Plan 235's `docs.rs` table already holds every `docs/cli` file listed at `cargo test` time, but that test rebuilds the binary first, so it cannot see drift between a build and an edit; this stage can. When the type pages come from the daemon's type catalog (blueprint 005 c-type-catalog), their source is that catalog's file and the same comparison applies.

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Cost: no loop, poll, timer or hook. On demand only, inside `harness checks`: one `pij-rs docs list` and one `pij-rs docs get` per bundled page (a handful today), absolute-path launches of the built binary; no daemon contact. Scales with pages, not seats.
